name: Temporal Frequency Anomaly
description: Detects anomalous temporal frequency signatures in video — AI generation creates distinctive temporal spectral patterns.
mechanism:
This method detects temporal frequency anomalies for video deepfake detection:

1. **Temporal Signal Extraction**: Per-pixel or per-region temporal signals are extracted — tracking intensity, color, and texture over time. These signals capture the temporal dynamics at each spatial location.

2. **Temporal Frequency Decomposition**: Temporal signals are analyzed via FFT to obtain per-location temporal frequency spectra. This reveals the frequency components of temporal variation: scene motion (~0-5 Hz), lighting changes (~0-1 Hz), and potential generation artifacts.

3. **Anomaly Detection in Temporal Spectra**: Natural video temporal spectra are dominated by low frequencies (slow scene changes) with rapid falloff at higher frequencies. The method detects anomalous spectral components: (a) energy at incommensurate frequencies with no physical source, (b) spectral peaks at the video generator's characteristic temporal frequencies, (c) unexpected harmonics from repetitive generation patterns.

4. **Spatial Mapping of Temporal Anomalies**: The detected temporal frequency anomalies are mapped spatially. Anomalies concentrated in face regions (but absent in background) strongly indicate face-specific generation artifacts. The spatial distribution of temporal anomalies reveals the extent and boundaries of generated content.

5. **Cross-Frequency Coherence**: In natural video, temporal frequency components at different spatial frequencies are coherently related (same physical motion produces correlated temporal variations at all spatial frequencies). The method checks cross-frequency coherence — AI generation may produce temporally incoherent variations at different spatial scales.
parameters: Analysis type: automated statistical\nScore range: 0 (authentic) to 100 (AI-generated)\nMinimum input size: varies by media type
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% accuracy depending on input quality and method combination.
source: Based on peer-reviewed research in digital forensics and AI content detection.
useCase: Used as part of multi-signal analysis pipeline to detect AI-generated content.
strengths:
• Research-backed methodology
• Fast computation time
• Complementary to other detection methods
• Works across different AI generators
limitations: • Accuracy varies with input quality\n• Best used in combination with other methods\n• May require calibration for new AI models
